page: Microsoft Azure F4s_v2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FSv2 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. This instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes 33 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the F4s_v2 delivers modest performance across various compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests falls into the bottom 25% tier, with scores of 1409.49 and 3661.48 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak throughput, measuring 25.4 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 20.93 GB/sec for large-block write operations. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 23.8 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.02 GB/sec. Geekbench testing aligns with these findings, showing an average single-core score of 1144.0 but a weak multi-core score of 2517.0.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F4s_v2 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for tasks where CPU allocation is prioritized over memory capacity. However, the low memory bandwidth and weak database operations performance present a clear tradeoff for data-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and entry-level development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU resources without high memory demands.
